newsitem.title: USA: Rains slow Okla wheat harvest, 65 percent complete.
newsitem.headline: Rains slow Okla wheat harvest, 65 percent complete.

text.p: Scattered showers interfered with wheat harvest activities in many areas of the state in the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its crop progress report.

"Harvest increased by less than 20 percentage points in southern and eastern Oklahoma as well as the Panhandle," the report said. "Test weights were holding strong and yields were better than expected."
Statewide, harvest was 65 percent complete, compared with 83 percent for the five-year average. Nineteen percent had been plowed versus the 38 percent average.

Corn was rated two percent poor, seven percent fair, 89 percent good and two percent excellent. Ten percent of the crop was tasseling, against 35 percent on average. Two percent was in the milk to soft dough stage, versus eight percent average.
Sorghum was rated one percent poor, 12 percent fair, 85 percent good and two percent excellent. The crop was 91 percent planted, against 89 percent for the five-year average.
Soybeans were rated 63 percent good to excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated nil very short, nine percent short, 78 percent adequate and 13 percent surplus.
